transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you lately that brought you in today?

I guess I'm here because the clinic doctor got on my case about my eating. I don't really see the big deal, honestly. Most days I just keep it simple—coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between painting jobs, and a small dinner if I'm not too tied up with my college coursework. It just works for me.
Do you worry about gaining weight or feel like your body is bigger than it actually is?

Yeah, I do worry about it. I mean, if I eat something heavy—like pizza or a big sandwich—I get this really panicky feeling. It's like I'm scared I'll just wake up bigger and slower. And with my job, I have to be light on my feet. I need to be able to move up and down ladders and navigate tight rooms the way I need to for painting. So, yeah, the idea of gaining weight and not being able to move around like that definitely stresses me out.
After eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, take laxatives, or exercise more than usual to prevent weight gain?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything. And I don't really exercise outside of work. Painting all day is pretty physical on its own, so I don't feel the need to do extra workouts or anything like that. I just try to control it by not eating too much in the first place.
